invariants.statement: The name starts out empty and the game fills the name from the saved variables file.
The game loads the file before the compiled add-on rather than compiling the two together.

value.definition: an environment that answers to every name the game's own Lua would reach for

invariants.statement: A name the environment does not know answers with a stub.
A stub answers to being called.
A stub answers to being joined onto text as the empty string.
A stub answers to arithmetic as zero.
A stub reached for a field answers with another stub.
A name the caller bans answers with nothing.
A banned name is taken off the real globals as well.
A game function known to answer text answers with the empty string.
A game function known to answer a count answers with zero.
A game constant the loaded Lua branches on has the value the game gives that constant.
Loaded Lua runs with this environment in place of the real globals.
A value seeded by the caller is read before any stub is made.

value.definition: the loop a Lua subprocess runs, reading scripts in and writing answers back

invariants.statement: A script arrives as lines closed by a run sentinel of its own.
An answer is one JSON document closed by a done sentinel of its own.
An answer says whether the script ran and has either a value or an error.
A script that fails to compile answers as an error rather than ending the loop.
A script that throws answers as an error rather than ending the loop.
A table whose keys start at 1 and rise with no gap is written as a JSON array.
Every other table is written as a JSON object.
A number JSON cannot have is written as a tagged object.
A function is written as a tagged object rather than as a value.
Closed input ends the loop.
